observations: Photos show a white plastic IBC (intermediate bulk container) with a black steel cage and top lifting frame.
Photo 1 shows a blue outlet/valve area at the bottom corner and a label/sticker on the tank front-right.
Photo 2 is a close-up of the tank wall; there are visible scuffs/marks and faint surface discoloration, but no obvious crack is clearly visible in the image.
No clear readable brand/model/IBC capacity marking is visible in the provided photos.

claims.claim: To store industrial liquids or hazardous chemicals
claims.evidence: Photos show an IBC tank, but do not show certification/UN rating or chemical compatibility markings.
No clearly readable food-grade/NSF/FDA/UN/DOT or dedicated food-contact marking is visible in the photos.

claims.claim: Used only once for clean water
claims.evidence: Photos do not confirm prior contents; only surface marks are visible.

claims.claim: No crack, no leak, lids complete
claims.evidence: No leak test is shown; lids/closures are not clearly shown in a way that confirms completeness.

risks.risk: Food-grade status may be false; tank may have previously held non-food chemicals or may not be certified for food contact.
risks.proof: Clear photo of the IBC label/markings showing food-grade certification (e.g., NSF/food-contact) and prior-use/compatibility info; also photo of the bung/lid markings.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a general-purpose used IBC (not food-grade).

risks.risk: Leak risk: seller claims no leak, but photos cannot confirm seals, valve condition, or micro-cracks.
risks.proof: Video/clip of a pressure/leak test or a fill-and-hold test (showing no drips around valve, bottom outlet, and seams) plus close-ups of the valve and gasket.
risks.if_unproven: Price as potentially needing inspection/repair (assume not guaranteed leak-free).

risks.risk: Capacity/size unknown; price depends heavily on whether it’s 1000L/IBC standard or another size.
risks.proof: Photo of the capacity marking (e.g., 1000L) on the IBC data plate/label.
risks.if_unproven: Price at the worst-case assumption for value (standard used IBC without confirmed capacity).

risks.risk: Condition of the cage and tank: scuffs/marks may indicate rough handling; structural damage could reduce usability.
risks.proof: Full 360° photos of the steel cage welds and the tank corners/bottom, plus close-up of any dents or deformations.
risks.if_unproven: Price as used with cosmetic wear (and assume no structural guarantee).

proof_requests: Clear photo of the IBC data plate/label showing capacity (e.g., 1000L), material type, and any certification/food-grade markings.
Close-up photos of the top lid(s)/closures and the bottom outlet valve assembly (including gaskets/seals).
Video of a leak test (fill with water and show no drips for a short hold period), especially around the valve and seams.
Full 360° condition photos of tank corners, bottom, and steel cage weld points.
response.reason: It’s clearly an IBC tank, but key pricing drivers (food-grade certification, confirmed leak-free condition, and capacity marking) are not verifiable from the photos. Without those, the correct worst-case pricing cannot be confidently set.
